ecommerce_adapter_boundary.principle: LOCKED 2026-07-20 (owner). We support WooCommerce PRECISELY SO the site owner can run any payment gateway, any coupon plugin, any currency plugin, any tax plugin — without us knowing or caring. From an adapter, exactly ONE fact matters: is the platform order COMPLETE or not.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.what_we_read_from_the_platform: Completion status (paid / refunded, and how much was refunded). The platform order id, for reference. That is the contract surface.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.they_are_payment_RAILS_not_platforms: LOCKED 2026-07-21 (owner): 'Woo is just a payment gateway for us like Stripe or PayPal.' WooCommerce, EDD, SureCart and FluentCart are payment RAILS, exactly like Stripe and PayPal — they report whether money moved, and we own the order semantics. They do NOT get their own status vocabulary that we translate: Stripe does not tell us to call an order 'cancelled', it tells us a refund succeeded and WE decide the order is 'refunded'. Woo gets identical treatment. Consequence: status MAPS are the wrong shape — see the refunded->cancelled map at Pro WCOrderProvider.php:487, scheduled for retirement in audit/REFUND-PLAN.md D4.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.the_rail_never_changes_the_numbers: LOCKED 2026-07-21 (owner): the gateway 'should not impact how we are calculating earning and refunds.' The rail decides only WHETHER money moved and HOW MUCH the buyer got back; it never influences arithmetic. Order total comes from our service/package price (never the rail's line total); platform_fee and vendor_earnings from CommissionService::compute_breakdown(); the vendor share of a refund from wpss_get_refund_vendor_share(); ledger rows from reverse_order_earnings(); amounts stored in base currency. A $49 service refunded in full reverses the same vendor share whether the buyer paid via Woo, Stripe, PayPal, EDD or SureCart. If swapping the rail changes any persisted number, that is the bug — not a configuration difference. This is why Pro must own no reverse_* or fee math of its own: per-rail money logic is exactly how the numbers drift apart.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.what_we_do_NOT_read: Charged amount, currency, coupon/discount, tax, gateway, fees. Reading any of those couples us to whatever plugin the owner installed and puts foreign values into our order rows, our commission split and our ledger.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.what_we_price_from: OUR OWN service/package price, always. A $49 service is a $49 order — completed is completed. Vendor earnings and the commission split are computed from our list price and never move because a buyer used a coupon, switched currency, or paid through a different gateway.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.consequence_owner_accepted: Discounts and FX differences are absorbed by the PLATFORM OWNER, not the vendor. The vendor is still paid on the list price they set. This is not a tradeoff under the current model — ONLY THE ADMIN can issue a discount (e.g. a 10% special offer); vendors have no coupon capability. The party running the promotion is therefore the party funding it, which is correct by construction. It also keeps vendor earnings predictable and the ledger in one unit.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.REVISIT_IF: Vendor-level coupons are ever introduced. At that point 'owner absorbs the discount' stops being obviously correct: a vendor's own promotion should reduce that vendor's earnings, not the owner's margin, which means the adapter would need to distinguish an admin discount from a vendor discount. Until then, do not read discounts from the platform at all. Anyone reading this and thinking 'the vendor is overpaid on discounted orders' has found the intended behaviour, not a bug.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.why_services_are_not_products: The underlying reason this model differs from normal ecommerce: we sell SERVICES, not physical stock. A service price is a vendor's rate for their own labour and delivery commitment — not a retail SKU price subject to margin, inventory or promotional dynamics. Discounting a service does not make the work smaller, so the vendor's side of the transaction is fixed at their listed rate and the discount is a platform-side marketing cost. Reasoning about this code as if it were a product store is the main way people get it wrong.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.why_this_is_the_right_seam: It is also why the adapter layer exists at all (wpss_ecommerce_adapters). Every time an adapter reaches past 'is it complete?' into the platform's money, it re-couples us to that platform's plugin ecosystem and imports a class of bugs we cannot test against. See money_authorities.currency_storage.KNOWN_GAP_woo_path_contradicts_this for a live instance.
ecommerce_adapter_boundary.applies_to: WooCommerce, EDD, SureCart, FluentCart adapters equally.

money_authorities._note: READ THIS BEFORE TOUCHING ANY MONEY PATH. There is exactly one authority per concept — plus one UNRESOLVED split flagged below. See also ecommerce_adapter_boundary, which governs what an adapter may read from the host platform at all.

commission.rule: Never compute a fee inline. Free (ManualOrderPage, OrderWorkflowManager) and Pro (TieredCommission flat rules, SubscriptionManager plan override, Stripe Connect split, EDD orders, subscription renewals) all route through it; the Connect split reads the PERSISTED fee and never recomputes.

wallet_balance.rule: SUM over {prefix}wpss_wallet_transactions, 'pending' rows excluded. Never SUM the table inline; pass $lock = true inside a credit/debit transaction to take FOR UPDATE. Replaced the stale vendor_profiles balance column (free) and three divergent SUM copies (Pro) in 1.2.2.
wallet_balance.callers: free: VendorsPage x3, CommissionService, OrderWorkflowManager, MilestoneService, ExtensionOrderService, TippingService; pro: InternalWalletProvider x3

payout_terminal.rule: THE terminal step of every payout rail (MONEY-FLOW.md rule 2.3). Row-locks the withdrawal (SELECT … FOR UPDATE), enforces the terminal-state guard, flips status to completed and writes the wallet-ledger debit in ONE transaction via the private insert_withdrawal_debit() core. Idempotent: marking twice debits once. process_withdrawal('completed'), the admin Withdrawals page (single + bulk) and REST PUT /wpss/v1/withdrawals/{id} all route through it — no rail may keep its own bookkeeping. record_withdrawal_debit() remains the transactional wrapper for the wpss_withdrawal_processed hook listener and the 1.2.3 backfill, both idempotent on (reference_type='withdrawal', reference_id).
payout_terminal.export_rule: CSV export (WithdrawalsPage::export_csv via admin_post_wpss_export_withdrawals) NEVER mutates status (rule 2.4) — SELECT-only, keyset-batched at 500 rows.

currency_storage.decision: LOCKED 2026-07-20 (owner). Every amount this plugin persists is a SINGLE value in the store's BASE currency. Full stop.
currency_storage.rule: wpss_orders (total, platform_fee, vendor_earnings) and wpss_wallet_transactions.amount are always base currency. We do NOT store a second shopper-currency amount, and we do NOT persist an exchange rate. There is no dual-currency order row.
currency_storage.boundary: Converting is the MULTI-CURRENCY PLUGIN's responsibility (CURCY / Aelia / WCML) — exactly as it already is for WooCommerce. Those plugins do not rewrite Woo's storage; they hook Woo's price filters and hand Woo converted values. We are a consumer on the same terms: whatever reaches our storage is already base currency, and display conversion is theirs.
currency_storage.integration_seam: The actionable consequence: WPSS price reads need filter seams equivalent to Woo's price filters, so a multi-currency plugin can hook us the same way it hooks Woo, rather than needing WPSS-specific support. Service and package prices currently come straight out of post meta (_wpss_packages price, _wpss_starting_price) with no filter, which is precisely why card 10110476797 reports a base number wearing a converted symbol. Add the seam; do not add conversion logic of our own.
currency_storage.why: The ledger and vendor payouts aggregate across many orders; that only works in one stable unit. Storing shopper-currency amounts would make wpss_get_ledger_balance() sum mixed units, and would force every payout, withdrawal and Connect split to become currency-aware. Woo core is itself single-currency (one currency column on the order, no rate anywhere in core) — multi-currency is plugin territory there too, so this keeps the boundary where Woo already draws it.
currency_storage.consequence: wpss_wallet_transactions.currency is expected to hold ONE value per install (the base currency). wpss_get_ledger_balance() sums without a currency filter, which is correct under this contract and only correct under this contract — if mixed currencies ever appear in that table, the balance is arithmetic nonsense and the bug is upstream, at whatever wrote a non-base row.
currency_storage.rejected: The card's original proposal (store base currency + the rate used, convert for display) and the store-both variant were both considered and rejected as more machinery than this plugin needs.
currency_storage.worked_example: A $49 service is a $49 order, always. Whatever the shopper actually paid on the Woo store, in whatever currency, is Woo's business — our order row, our commission split and our ledger all read $49. A vendor's earnings on a service never change because a buyer switched currency.
currency_storage.card: Basecamp 10110476797 — item 3 of that card is now answered; items 1 and 2 reduce to exposing price filter seams, and item 4 (persist the refund rate) is dropped entirely under this contract.
currency_storage.RESOLVED_woo_path: FIXED 2026-07-22 (Pro 4a48c11). WCOrderProvider used to build the order from Woo's amounts — $item->get_total() / _line_total for the price and $order->get_currency() for the currency — so the vendor's earnings depended on how the buyer paid and shopper-currency amounts flowed into a ledger that sums without a currency filter. Now reads OUR _wpss_packages price via get_package_price_by_id() and stores the base currency from the raw woocommerce_currency option. Deliberately NOT wpss_get_currency(), which Pro 1.2.2 made defer to get_woocommerce_currency() — the value CURCY/Aelia filter to the shopper's currency. Verified: a Woo line charging 31.75 EUR against our 50.00 package yields 50.00, and with woocommerce_currency filtered to EUR the stored currency stays USD.

currency_conversion.rule: Never multiply by 100 inline when talking to a gateway, and never compare gateway amounts with a hardcoded epsilon. Zero-decimal (JPY) and 3-decimal (BHD/JOD/KWD/OMR/TND) currencies both break the naive form.

withdrawable_balance.authority: EarningsService::get_summary()['available_balance'] — and it derives from the wallet ledger.
withdrawable_balance.formula: available = wpss_get_ledger_balance() - pending_withdrawal - in_clearance. The ledger is ALREADY net of completed withdrawals, so completed payouts must never be subtracted again. 'pending_withdrawal' covers still-open requests (pending + approved) that have not reached the ledger yet. 'in_clearance' is the sum of ledger CREDIT rows inside the clearance window.
withdrawable_balance.rule: Never re-derive a balance inline. Both prior inline copies are gone: EarningsController::get_summary (REST) and the withdrawal-request gate in EarningsController::create_withdrawal now both call EarningsService::get_summary().
withdrawable_balance.history: Until 1.2.3 this was a SECOND authority — it summed vendor_earnings over completed orders and never consulted the ledger, so any ledger entry with no matching order row (manual adjustment, tip credit, order reversal) moved one number and not the other. A vendor was shown one balance and gated on another. Resolved 2026-07-20 (ledger wins).
withdrawable_balance.withdrawal_debits: Completed withdrawals are debited into the ledger by EarningsService::record_withdrawal_debit(), wired to wpss_withdrawal_processed in FREE (Plugin.php). It used to live only in Pro's WalletManager, so a free-only site paid vendors out without ever debiting them and the same install grew a different balance depending on whether Pro was active. Pro's listener is now removed to avoid a double debit; idempotency matches on (reference_type='withdrawal', reference_id) so Pro's existing type='debit' rows are recognised.
withdrawable_balance.upgrade_migration: EarningsService::backfill_withdrawal_debits() runs once on upgrade to 1.2.3 (Plugin::maybe_run_install). Without it, installs that never wrote withdrawal debits would read HIGH by everything already paid out and vendors could withdraw it twice. Idempotent and safe to re-run.
withdrawable_balance.clearance_note: Clearance is now derived from ledger row created_at rather than orders.completed_at, so tips, milestone and extension credits observe the clearance window too — the orders-derived version exempted all three.
withdrawable_balance.also_dead: {prefix}wpss_vendor_profiles.available_balance / .pending_balance are mutated by a raw UPDATE at src/Frontend/AjaxHandlers.php:3405 but read by NO balance path. Write-only columns — safe to retire.
withdrawable_balance.also_note: wpss_wallet_transactions.balance_after IS still read — Pro's LedgerExporter (src/Services/LedgerExporter.php) selects it for statement CSVs. Retiring the column requires giving the exporter a running-balance computation first.

money_authorities.refunded_amount_display: wpss_get_order_refunded_amount( object $order ): float in src/functions.php is THE ONLY way a display, invoice or export surface may ask how much was refunded. wpss_orders.refunded_amount stores a SENTINEL, not a plain number: NULL means 'fully refunded', a value means 'this much was refunded'. That sentinel is load-bearing for the money layer (OrderWorkflowManager::settle_refund reads NULL as 'reverse everything', DisputeService::persist_refunded_amount writes NULL for full refunds) and MUST NOT be changed to store the total. The hazard is read-side: templates/order/order-view.php read the raw column and tested `> 0`, which silently dropped every FULL refund - the buyer saw the status 'Refunded' with no amount beside it, while a PARTIAL refund correctly showed one. Its own is_full_refund branch was dead code. The helper disambiguates 'full refund' from 'no refund' via order status and returns 0.0 when nothing was refunded. Never read the column directly from a template. Commit 2dc698b.

generated.refresh_note: 1.3.1 refresh (hand-edited; manifest_refresh: agent-enumeration-only — do NOT run write-manifest.mjs against this plugin, it undercounts REST 138->7 and clobbers the file). Deltas this cycle: (1) Payment ownership is exclusive — PaymentController registers only when wpss_uses_standalone_payments() (src/API/PaymentController.php:55), so /payments/* is absent whenever a cart adapter is active; switching rails never rewrites past orders. (2) New pay-order seam: helper wpss_get_pay_order_url() + filter wpss_pay_order_url (src/functions.php:3375/3391), the single source for 'pay THIS order' across tips, milestone phases, extensions, accepted proposals, order templates, REST checkout_url and emails. Only Pro's WCPayOrderResolver implements it; EDD/FluentCart/SureCart have no pay-order rail. (3) Minor-unit integers beside every money float. (4) Notification bodies plain text; HTML composed only for email. (5) REST: added GET /orders/{id}/timeline, GET /auth/devices, POST /reviews (alias), GET /portfolio, GET /media; REMOVED the dead accept|reject order actions from the /orders/{id}/{action} enum and with them the hooks wpss_order_accepted, wpss_order_rejected, wpss_order_delivered; deliver now routes through DeliveryService. (6) REST auth answers 401 vs 403 correctly via wpss_rest_require_login()/wpss_rest_require_admin() with one wpss_not_vendor code (bare boolean permission callbacks made anonymous callers read as rest_forbidden). (7) i18n build generates .mo/.json catalogs with a CI gate. Docs: docs-audit.py extended to scan docs/architecture, docs/qa and docs/decisions, to check 'Sell Services > X' menu paths as well as 'Settings > X' tabs, and to name the retired tab/menu labels explicitly. || 1.6.0 delta (cards 10208094640 + 10208199238): ServiceOrder::get_service() guards service_id <= 0 and post_type (get_post(0) returned the global post, so proposal/sub-orders resolved their service to the rendering page); new wpss_get_order_subject() is the single resolver for an order's subject line across the admin list, admin order detail, admin dashboard and frontend order view; new wpss_record_pending_payment_method() records the chosen rail on an unsettled order and is called by both offline entry points (AJAX checkout + REST /payments/create-intent), which previously left payment_method NULL and made the order impossible to confirm. No REST routes added or removed; PaymentController::create_offline_order can now answer 500 wpss_payment_method_not_recorded. || 1.6.0 delta (cards 10208211608 + 10208142348, one shape: a guard hid a CTA and nothing replaced it): admin order detail now surfaces the order's dispute via DisputeService::get_by_order() (loud while unresolved, quiet once closed, with an explicit warning when a Completed order still carries a live dispute); the order page's review block now renders the submitted review instead of nothing, gates the CTA and the modal on the single ReviewService::can_review() authority so the review window is respected, and explains itself when the CTA is withheld. New shared partial templates/partials/review-body.php renders a Review model and is used by both the order page and the public reviews list, which previously had its own inline copy reading raw columns. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10208211769): new wpss_get_settings_url() + wpss_get_settings_sections() (filter wpss_settings_sections); all 13 `&tab=` settings deep links in Free and Pro converted to hash routing, and FIVE of them additionally pointed at the wrong section - verified against each feature's real settings render hook, not the old link (Stripe Connect and Razorpay named 'gateways' which never existed -> payments; PayPal Payouts payments -> payouts; Tiered Commission payments -> commission; Recurring Services vendor -> orders). admin-settings-nav.js gained legacy ?tab= support and hashchange handling; .min rebuilt. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10208142467): Become a Vendor now gates on wpss_is_vendor() instead of the raw _wpss_is_vendor meta, which was falsy for every role-granted vendor; VendorService::is_vendor() delegates to the same helper instead of re-deriving role-then-meta (it was missing the capability path and the wpss_is_vendor filter); a dead raw-meta read removed from AjaxHandlers::save_profile. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10208075268): the unread COUNT was correct and invisible - the badge's text-indent: -999999px rendered it as a bare dot, so it now shows the number (capped at 99+) with a title/screen-reader label naming whose messages it counts; badge suppressed on closed threads so the badges sum to the banner; the messages list is paginated via new count_conversations_for_user() + the wpss_messages_per_page filter, using an explicit wpss_paged arg because the default pretty base 404s on the section-routed dashboard; dead ConversationRepository::create_conversation()/add_message() removed, eliminating a second participants shape and an array_keys() iterator that would have credited unread to users 0 and 1. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10208199338): the leftover published /create-service/ page - a virtual route that older installs materialised as a real, empty page - now 302s to the dashboard create section where the wizard actually lives, and is de-indexed and dropped from the sitemap. Implemented by generalising the existing dormant-page mechanism (get_dormant_store_page_ids -> get_dormant_page_ids, now memoised) rather than adding a second redirect path; a page the owner has mapped in Settings > Pages is exempt. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10207973462): new WPSS.syncStickyTop() measures the real pinned chrome (admin bar + theme header, which stack) into --wpss-sticky-top instead of assuming admin-bar-only, as a floor over the CSS value so no-theme-header sites are unchanged; recomputed on resize/scroll/load; new wpss_sticky_top_offset PHP filter for headers the measurement cannot see. || 1.6.0: losing-bidder emails suppressed for the hire-someone-else path (in-app only, owner decision); explicit rejections still email. Verified live: hiring 1 of 3 proposals produced 2 in-app 'Proposal not selected' notifications, 1 acceptance notification and exactly 1 email (the winner's); an explicit reject produced 1 email + 1 notification. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10138985537): new js-fallback check in bin/i18n-verify.py (both plugins, byte-identical) catching a localized-key fallback whose PHP key no longer exists; new jsFallbackAllowedKeys config; Pro's CI now runs the i18n gate it already shipped but never executed; Pro POT regenerated. || 1.6.0 delta (card 10208511245): dual H1 on cart and dashboard fixed - `cart` added to ShellHeader's shell surfaces and the in_the_loop() requirement dropped from the_title suppression (BuddyX renders its entry-title outside the loop); new restore_nav_menu_item_title() repairs the one nav-menu label suppression would blank; the cart shortcode's logged-out and rail-redirect branches and the dashboard's login prompt now render ShellHeader::render(), since adding a page to the shell means it must have its own H1 in EVERY branch. checkout/become_vendor/vendors_page deliberately NOT added - they have only the theme's H1. || 1.6.0 RFD card 10163575694: account-at-checkout (setting wpss_general[checkout_account_creation], OFF by default). New wp_ajax_nopriv_wpss_checkout_create_account; PublicSignup::create_account() is now the single account path and REST /auth/register delegates to it with username/password optional; RateLimiter gains 'checkout_account'. ALSO FIXED, found while testing: sanitize_general() defaulted absent keys, so ANY partial update_option('wpss_general') silently reset platform_name, currency, checkout_badges_enabled and - critically - ecommerce_platform to 'auto', moving the site's PAYMENT RAIL. Reproduced by a one-key `wp option patch`, which flipped a standalone site to EDD.

portfolio_standards.account_billing_layer: ~/.claude/workflows/wbcom-account-billing-standard.md — LOCKED 2026-07-22. Applies to EVERY Wbcom plugin that takes money, not just this one. Billing identity lives on the USER via WooCommerce's billing_* meta keys (plus billing_gst, which Woo lacks), so one address is shared across Learnomy, Eventonomy, WP Sell Services, Career Board, Listora and BuddyNext with no cross-plugin dependency. Orders snapshot the address at payment so invoices cannot be rewritten by a later profile edit. Gateways CONSUME the values, never render or own them. Country and currency lists must be COMPLETE and come from one helper each — a partial list silently excludes customers rather than failing visibly. This plugin is the reference implementation.
portfolio_standards.reference_implementation: wpss_get_billing_fields() / wpss_get_billing_address() / wpss_save_billing_address() / wpss_is_billing_address_complete() / wpss_get_countries() / wpss_get_currency_registry() in src/functions.php; wpss_orders.billing_address JSON snapshot; templates/partials/billing-fields.php. Commits a86b867, 7655e99, d97f1f0, b6d18c4.
portfolio_standards.billing_display_authority: templates/partials/billing-summary.php is THE ONLY read-only billing renderer — buyer order view (templates/order/order-view.php), admin order screen (Admin::render_order_detail) and any future invoice/export all include this one partial, so the customer and the admin can never be shown different invoice detail. It accepts BOTH shapes billing_address arrives in (ServiceOrder decodes to array; admin passes a raw $wpdb row where it is still a JSON string) rather than forcing callers to hydrate a model. It reads the ORDER SNAPSHOT only and never falls back to the live profile — a fallback would show an address the buyer was not billed under. Pre-1.5.0 orders have no snapshot and render nothing. Editable counterpart is billing-fields.php; the two must stay in step. Styled in design-system.css AND admin.css because design-system.css is not enqueued in wp-admin. Commit 894161d.

hooks._note: Unique do_action()/apply_filters() literals in src/. Counts enumerated by hand for 1.3.1 and NOT re-counted since; treat as indicative, not exact. key_extension_hooks below is maintained per-change and is authoritative for documented seams.

notifications._note: In-app notifications live in {prefix}wpss_notifications. NotificationService::create() is the ONE writer (it also persists action_url, the deep link) and NotificationService::send() maps a type to its title/body copy -- add a `case` there for any new type or it silently renders the generic 'You have a new notification.' fallback. Domain event -> notification wiring lives in Plugin::define_notification_hooks(). A type that emails via EmailService MUST also be listed in NotificationService::is_email_service_handling()'s $covered_types, or the recipient gets the branded mail plus a plain duplicate.
notifications.deep_link_column: action_url (written by create() from $data['action_url'], rendered as the row title link)
notifications.known_drift: Notification::get_icon() is keyed on TYPE_* constants ('order_new', 'message_new') that are largely never written; the live icon map is in the render partial. Unifying them is an open item.
notifications.losing_bidder_policy: Owner decision 2026-08-17: a seller who loses because someone else was hired gets an IN-APP notification and NO email. Before 1.6.0 reject_other_proposals() bulk-UPDATEd their rows and fired nothing, so they were told nothing at all; fixing that meant hiring on a request with 200 proposals would fire 199 notifications AND 199 emails inside the buyer's single click - enough to time the request out and to trip a host's mail limit. ProposalService::reject_other_proposals() sets `wpss_not_selected = true` on the proposal it passes to wpss_proposal_rejected, and EmailService::send_proposal_rejected() returns early on it. NotificationService does not, so every loser is still told. An EXPLICIT rejection (ProposalService::reject(), where the buyer picked that seller and usually wrote a reason) still emails - one message, not a burst. Deliberately a property rather than a second action name: wpss_proposal_rejected has been the event since 1.0.0 and Pro / customer listeners must keep firing, and a fourth argument would not reach EmailService, whose handler is registered with three.

disputes._note: A dispute conversation is ONE store: {prefix}wpss_dispute_messages. It used to be two -- the opening statement and admin replies in that table, member evidence in the disputes row's `evidence` JSON -- and each surface read only one, so members saw 'No messages yet' on a thread the admin could read in full, and admins never saw member evidence. DisputeService::add_evidence() writes the table; get_evidence() reads it and is the single reader (DisputeWorkflowManager::get_timeline() consumes it rather than querying again, or every message would appear twice). The `evidence` column now holds ONLY status_note entries written by update_status() -- dispute status history, not conversation. Legacy rows are moved by DisputeService::migrate_evidence_to_messages(), gated on the wpss_dispute_evidence_migrated option.
disputes.order_surface: src/Admin/Admin.php::render_order_detail -- dispute banner on the order itself (notice-error while open/pending_review/escalated, notice-info once resolved/closed), via DisputeService::get_by_order(). A dispute does NOT force the order's status, so a Completed order can carry an open dispute; this screen previously showed status, messages, deliveries and refund controls with no mention of it (Basecamp 10208211608).
disputes.reason_column_is_free_text: wpss_disputes.reason holds free text on real installs ('Quality issue', 'rft'), not only the Dispute::REASON_* keys. Any label lookup MUST fall through to the raw value -- confirmed against sandbox rows, which contradicted the enum the code implies.

orders._note: An order does not always point at a service post. Buyer-request orders are sold off a proposal and every sub-order (tip, extension, milestone) hangs off a parent, so all of them carry service_id = 0 BY DESIGN. get_post( 0 ) returns the GLOBAL $post rather than null, so ServiceOrder::get_service() used to resolve those orders' "service" to whatever page was rendering -- on the checkout page a proposal order reported the checkout page as its service (title "Service Checkout", form posting the page ID as service_id), and in wp-admin, where there is no global post, the same orders read "Deleted". Every `if ( ! $service )` fallback in the plugin was therefore unreachable. get_service() now guards service_id <= 0 and checks post_type, and one resolver -- wpss_get_order_subject() -- answers "what is this order for" for all four surfaces that used to answer it differently.
orders.service_resolver: WPSellServices\Models\ServiceOrder::get_service (returns null for service_id <= 0; requires post_type wpss_service)
subject_resolution_order: platform 'request' -> the wpss_request post, else meta.proposal_snapshot.request_title, else 'Buyer request'
service_id <= 0 on a catalog order -> 'No service linked' (data integrity, not a deletion)
subject_surfaces: src/Admin/Admin.php (admin order detail + admin dashboard Recent Orders)
orders.subject_known_drift: templates/dashboard/sections/orders.php and sales.php still build their own card title. They are correct (they guard service_id before get_post and fall back to the request post) and add milestone phase titles the resolver does not own, so they were left alone -- but they remain a second implementation of the same label.
orders.pending_payment_method_note: Gateways normally write payment_method as a side effect of mark_as_paid(). Offline does not settle in-request, so both of its pay-an-existing-order entry points (OfflineGateway::ajax_create_order and PaymentController::create_offline_order) go through this one guarded, idempotent writer. Leaving it NULL was a dead end, not a cosmetic gap: OfflineGateway::render_admin_order_actions(), PaymentReceiptService::can_submit() and the payment instructions all key off payment_method === 'offline', so the order could never be confirmed by anyone.
orders.payment_settlement_authority: StandaloneOrderProvider::mark_as_paid -- the only writer of payment_status/paid_at; wpss_record_pending_payment_method never touches them
orders.earnings_credit_timing: CommissionService::record() on transition to completed, not at payment (escrow model)

reviews._note: The order page's review block was `if ( ! $review_exists )` with no else, so the moment a buyer submitted a review the order went silent about it - the buyer's own review was invisible to the buyer on the only page they would look for it. The same seven lines also ran a raw $wpdb query for a question ReviewService already owns, and gated the CTA WITHOUT the review window, so after the window closed the button still invited a review the server would then refuse. can_review() is now the single authority on both the CTA and the modal, and its `reason` string is rendered when the CTA is withheld.
reviews.gate_authority: WPSellServices\Services\ReviewService::can_review( int $order_id, int $reviewer_id ): array{can_review: bool, reason: string} -- enforces completed + ownership + no-existing-review + within window
reviews.shared_partial: templates/partials/review-body.php -- author/stars/date header + content + seller response, takes a Review MODEL
shared_partial_consumers: templates/order/order-view.php (buyer sees 'Your Review', vendor sees 'Buyer Review')
templates/partials/service-reviews.php (public list; wraps raw rows with Review::from_db and keeps its own Helpful control)
reviews.model_shape_note: The reviews table columns and the model properties differ by name: review -> content, vendor_reply -> response, vendor_reply_at -> response_at, reviewee_id -> reviewed_id. There is NO title column. The public list used to read raw columns and used customer_id for the avatar while gating Helpful on reviewer_id - two names for one author on one screen. Everything now goes through Review::from_db().

vendor_identity._note: `_wpss_is_vendor` user meta is a LEGACY marker, not the answer to 'is this a vendor'. Vendors created by role assignment, by an admin, by the demo seeder, or by anything granting the wpss_vendor role do not carry it - on this sandbox that is EVERY vendor (all hold the role, none hold the meta). Reading the meta directly therefore answers 'not a vendor' for real sellers. The Become a Vendor page did exactly that and offered active sellers 'Register as Vendor' while their dashboard, services and earnings all worked (Basecamp 10208142467).
vendor_identity.canonical_check: wpss_is_vendor( ?int $user_id = null ) in src/functions/vendors.php -- capability wpss_vendor, then the wpss_vendor role, then the legacy meta, then the wpss_is_vendor filter
vendor_identity.service_wrapper: VendorService::is_vendor() delegates to wpss_is_vendor() as of 1.6.0. It previously checked role-then-meta itself, missing the capability path and the filter, so a capability-only vendor was a vendor everywhere except the dashboard and the service wizard.
legitimate_meta_writers: VendorService::register() / approve paths (write both role and meta)
vendor_identity.rule: Never read `_wpss_is_vendor` to gate a surface. Read it only when repairing or writing it.

messaging._note: The reported symptom (Basecamp 10208075268) was 'unread banner inflated; threads show own outbound as unread'. The COUNT was never wrong: Sofia's 15 was 9 + 6, and both were verified against sender_id counts to be messages from the other party. What was wrong was that the count was INVISIBLE - assets/css/unified-dashboard.css rendered the badge as a 12px dot with text-indent: -999999px, so the template wrote a number the stylesheet threw away. A dot beside a preview of your own last message reads as 'your own message is unread'.
messaging.participants_shape: ONE shape: a flat JSON list of user ids, [24,13]. Written by ConversationService::create_for_order() and create_direct().
messaging.unread_writer: ConversationService::send_message() - increments unread_counts for every participant except the sender
messaging.mark_read: ConversationRepository::mark_read - zeroes the user's unread_counts entry and stamps read_by on each message not sent by them
messaging.removed_in_1_6_0: ConversationRepository::create_conversation() and ::add_message() are GONE. Both had zero callers and between them held a second, incompatible participants shape (a MAP keyed by user id, array_fill_keys(...)) plus an iterator built on it: add_message() used foreach ( array_keys( $participants ) ), which on the real LIST shape yields the indices 0 and 1 - so if anything had ever called it, unread would have been credited to users 0 and 1 forever and never to the recipient. count_unread_for_user()'s docblock advertised the dual format and has been corrected.
messaging.pagination: count_conversations_for_user() + get_conversation_summary( $user_id, $limit, $offset ). The dashboard list was a hardcoded LIMIT 20 with no OFFSET, COUNT or navigation while the banner counted every conversation - one way a correct banner reads as inflated. Per page is filterable via wpss_messages_per_page (default 20).
messaging.pagination_query_arg: wpss_paged, NOT paged. The dashboard is a singular page with section routing (/dashboard/messages/), so WordPress does not populate `paged` and wpss_render_pagination()'s default pretty base (/dashboard/messages/page/2/) 404s - confirmed in the browser. The messages list passes an explicit base + format. NOTE: [wpss_my_orders] (src/Frontend/Shortcodes.php) still uses get_query_var('paged') with the default base and very likely has the same 404 when hosted on a page; not touched by this card.
messaging.closed_conversations: Shown in the list (history stays reachable) but never carry an unread badge, because count_unread_for_user() excludes them. Without that suppression the badges on screen and the banner disagreed.

dormant_pages._note: WPSS pages that are published but have nothing behind them. Never unpublished - old bookmarks, emailed ?pay_order=N links and the pages' own IDs still have to resolve - so they are 302'd to the live target, marked noindex and dropped from the WP core sitemap. A page an owner has MAPPED in Settings > Pages is never treated as dormant.
dormant_pages.resolver: WPSellServices\Core\Plugin::get_dormant_page_ids (memoised per request; was get_dormant_store_page_ids, renamed in 1.6.0 when it stopped being cart/checkout-only)

causes.cart + checkout: Seeded by the installer for the standalone rail and never removed, so they sit empty whenever WooCommerce/EDD/FluentCart/SureCart owns payment. Dormant ONLY on a non-standalone rail. Checkout resolves ?pay_order=N through wpss_get_pay_order_url() first so an emailed link reaches that order's real payment page.
causes.create_service: `create_service` is a VIRTUAL route: the dashboard renders it and it is deliberately absent from wpss_get_page_definitions(), so no current install creates a page. Installs upgraded from a version that DID create one keep a published, empty, unmapped page rendering no wizard (Basecamp 10208199338). Dormant on EVERY rail, and redirected to wpss_get_create_service_url() = the dashboard's create section.

dormant_pages.loop_guard: url_to_postid( $target ) === current page aborts the redirect, so a misconfiguration cannot loop.

sticky_offset._note: --wpss-sticky-top was admin-bar-only (32 / 64 / 78px) and knew nothing about the THEME's header, so every sticky WPSS surface pinned underneath a fixed theme header. Measured on BuddyX with its sticky header (which is ON by default, and becomes fixed once scrolled): header fixed at top 32px, 79px tall, occupying 32-111px, while the service sidebar pinned at 64px - 47px of it, including the package tabs, sat behind the header (Basecamp 10207973462).
sticky_offset.mechanism: WPSS.syncStickyTop() in assets/js/frontend.js measures every fixed/sticky top bar and writes the total into --wpss-sticky-top on <body>.
sticky_offset.why_not_css: The offset depends on a third party's header: it varies per theme, per breakpoint, and usually only becomes fixed (or changes height) on scroll. A selector cannot ask for it.
design_rules: Bars STACK: on an admin-bar site a fixed theme header sits at top: 32px, not 0. The measurement walks bars sorted by top and grows the region only while each starts where the last ended. A naive 'is it at the very top' test missed the header entirely - that was the first attempt, caught in the browser.
The result is a FLOOR over the CSS value, never a replacement, so a site with no theme header keeps exactly today's offset (verified: 64px, no inline override written).
Written to <body>, not :root - `.admin-bar` declares the variable on body, and a property on a descendant beats one on the ancestor.
WPSS's own sticky surfaces (STICKY_SURFACES) are excluded or the sidebar would measure itself and walk down the page.
Overlays, drawers and full-screen menus are excluded by height (> 40% of the viewport) and width (< 50%).
Recomputed on resize, scroll (rAF-throttled) and load, because themes shrink their header on scroll and a header measured before its webfont loads is short.
sticky_offset.gap: 16px of breathing room is added below the measured chrome.
sticky_offset.filter: wpss_sticky_top_offset (PHP, int px, default 0) - localized as wpssData.stickyTopOffset and ADDED to the measurement. The escape hatch for headers JS cannot see: positioned by transform, inside a shadow root, or another plugin's floating toolbar.
sticky_offset.consumers: design-system.css .wpss-sticky, single-service.css, orders.css, vendor-dashboard.css, buyer-request.css, messaging.css (viewport-height maths), frontend.css

i18n._note: Translation-READINESS (every user-facing string extractable and loadable), not shipped locales - shipping .po/.mo packs is out of scope. Basecamp 10138985537.
i18n.gate: bin/i18n-verify.py, byte-identical in Free and Pro, driven by .i18n-config.json in each plugin root

checks.version-drift: plugin header / POT Project-Id-Version / package.json / readme Stable tag must agree
checks.stale-pot: POT regenerated and diffed against source strings
checks.text-domain: every gettext call uses this plugin's domain
checks.script-i18n: every registered script handle has wp_set_script_translations
checks.js-fallback: NEW in 1.6.0: a JS `l10n.key || 'English'` whose key nothing localizes. The pattern is correct and deliberate - PHP owns the string, JS keeps a literal so a missing payload does not render `undefined`. It becomes permanent untranslatable English the moment the PHP key is renamed or dropped, and nothing looks broken. 54 had accumulated by 1.6.0 and were removed by hand; this is the check that stops them returning. Allowlist: jsFallbackAllowedKeys.

i18n.ci: Free: project-gates job. Pro: i18n-gate job, ADDED in 1.6.0 - Pro shipped the identical script in bin/ and never ran it, so its POT could go stale and its versions drift with a green build.
i18n.js_string_strategy: JS strings come from PHP via wp_localize_script (wpssData.i18n, wpssStripe.i18n, wpssRazorpay.i18n, ...), so they translate from the .mo with NO .json catalog needed. wp.i18n is used directly only in blocks.js/blocks-frontend.js. languages/*.json is generated by grunt i18n:json from .po files; with no shipped locales there are none to convert, which is the correct state, not a gap.
i18n.pro_script_pattern: Every Pro script with strings goes through Assets\ScriptRegistry::register/enqueue, which pairs wp_register_script with wp_set_script_translations atomically. Only third-party vendor libraries (lucide, chartjs, razorpay-checkout) are registered raw - they carry no translatable strings. Pro registers the FREE plugin's `wpss-icons` handle through FREE's registrar, so those strings resolve against the free domain.
i18n.verified_2026_08_17: Compiled a de_DE .mo for each plugin from its own POT and forced the locale. PHP: review CTA rendered '[de] Bewerten Sie Ihre Erfahrung' / '[de] Bewertung schreiben'. JS: wpssData.i18n.loading came back '[de] Wird geladen...', proving the PHP-localized JS path translates without JSON catalogs. Pro: the welcome page's Recurring Services badge rendered '[de] Demnaechst verfuegbar'. All scaffolding removed afterwards.

shell_header._note: One <h1> per plugin surface. The theme prints the WP page title as <h1 class="entry-title">; several plugin templates print their own. ShellHeader suppresses the theme's on surfaces where the plugin owns the heading (Basecamp 10208511245).
shell_header.class: WPSellServices\Frontend\ShellHeader, booted from Frontend::__construct on front-end requests
shell_header.shell_surfaces: wpss_is_page() for dashboard, services_page, cart -- ONLY pages that print their own H1 -- plus singular/archive wpss_service, its two taxonomies, singular/archive wpss_request, and the wpss_vendor query var.
shell_header.precondition: A page may only be added to the shell list once it renders its OWN heading. checkout, become_vendor and vendors_page are deliberately EXCLUDED: each has a single correct H1 today and it is the theme's, so suppressing it would leave the page with none. The card asked for all four to be added; three of them would have been a regression.
shell_header.auth_states_matter: The precondition must hold in EVERY branch, not just the happy path. Adding `cart` exposed two headingless pages: the cart shortcode's logged-out and rail-redirect branches returned before the template's H1, and UnifiedDashboard::render_login_prompt() only had an H2. Both now render ShellHeader::render().
shell_header.suppression: the_title filter. Guarded on is_main_query() + the id matching get_queried_object_id(). It does NOT require in_the_loop(): BuddyX renders its entry-title from a template part OUTSIDE the loop (probed: the_title fired 4x for the queried page, 3 of them with in_the_loop() false, and the heading that reached the screen was one of those).
shell_header.nav_menu_repair: ShellHeader::restore_nav_menu_item_title on wp_setup_nav_menu_item. wp_setup_nav_menu_item() builds a page item's label with get_the_title( $object_id ) -- same id, same filter -- so suppression made the menu's own 'Dashboard' item render as '#153 (no title)' while on the dashboard. The label is restored from the RAW post_title, only for the item pointing at the queried page, and only when the item carries no hand-written label of its own (read from the nav_menu_item post, since core may already have overwritten post_title with its placeholder).
rejected_approaches: A flag set around wp_nav_menu() to exempt menus: depends on when a theme renders its menu relative to its title. On BuddyX the flag was still set when the entry-title rendered, so the duplicate H1 returned. Measured, then abandoned.
Hiding .entry-title with CSS on the wpss-plugin-shell body class: leaves both headings in the accessibility tree, which is the actual defect.
shell_header.unaffected: Document <title> and BuddyX's breadcrumb current-page label both come from single_post_title(), which does not run through the_title. Breadcrumb ancestors, related-service cards and widgets carry other post ids and are guarded by the id match. All verified.
shell_header.filter: wpss_suppress_theme_title (bool) -- every return path in is_shell_surface() goes through it via filter_shell_surface(), so an early return cannot skip a site's override.
shell_header.verified_2026_08_17: 7 surfaces x logged-in and anonymous = 14 renders, each with exactly ONE h1, menu labels intact and no '(no title)' anywhere: cart 'Your Cart' (both states), checkout/become-a-vendor/vendors theme H1 untouched, dashboard 'Sales Orders' signed in and 'Access Your Dashboard' anonymous, services archive 'All Services', single service its own title.

checkout_account_creation._note: Basecamp 10163575694. There is NO guest order, by decision: after paying, a buyer must submit requirements, message the seller, review a delivery, request revisions and possibly open a dispute - all of which need an identity. An order with customer_id = 0 could not be fulfilled, and order access is checked as customer_id === get_current_user_id(), so a logged-out visitor IS user 0 and such an order would be readable by every logged-out visitor. Instead the sign-in WALL is removed and the account is created from the billing details the form already collects.
checkout_account_creation.setting: wpss_general['checkout_account_creation'], default OFF; helper wpss_checkout_creates_accounts(); filter of the same name
checkout_account_creation.no_new_fields: billing_first_name, billing_last_name and billing_email are the three LOCKED billing fields (wpss_get_required_billing_fields) - locked precisely because an order must be attributable to someone contactable. Checkout therefore gains no new inputs; the account is built from what the buyer was already typing.
checkout_account_creation.account_path: WPSellServices\Frontend\PublicSignup::create_account() - THE single account-creation path. The inline signup form, the checkout step and REST /auth/register all call it. AuthController::register() had its own wp_insert_user (no first/last name, no show_admin_bar_front, no wpss_public_signup_complete for Pro) and now delegates.
checkout_account_creation.endpoint: wp_ajax_nopriv_wpss_checkout_create_account -> PublicSignup::ajax_checkout_account(). Called by the checkout form BEFORE the payment request, so the order is inserted against a real customer_id.
checkout_account_creation.session_token_trap: wp_set_auth_cookie() only sends Set-Cookie; it does not touch $_COOKIE. wp_create_nonce() hashes wp_get_session_token(), which reads the logged-in cookie FROM $_COOKIE - so a nonce minted straight after signing in is built against an empty token while the browser's next request carries a real one, and the nonce fails. Hit on the first run: account created, fresh nonce returned, payment died on 'Security check failed'. create_account() now creates the session token explicitly, passes it to wp_set_auth_cookie() and writes $_COOKIE[LOGGED_IN_COOKIE].
checkout_account_creation.nonce_swap: The endpoint returns a fresh wpss_checkout nonce and the client swaps it before paying: WP nonces are user-bound, so the one rendered for a logged-out visitor stops verifying the instant they are signed in.
checkout_account_creation.email_collision: email_exists() -> 409 with code account_exists, a message and a login_url. No account, no order, NO charge. Attaching the order to the existing account would let anyone who knows an email drop an order into that person's history. The login URL is validated same-host, and the buyer gets a link rather than a redirect so a filled-in checkout is not thrown away. Owner-approved default.
checkout_account_creation.rate_limit: RateLimiter 'checkout_account', 20/hour keyed by IP. Deliberately generous: the key is an IP and behind CGNAT that can be a whole town, which is the customer this was asked for. Raise via wpss_rate_limits.
checkout_account_creation.scope: Single-service checkout ONLY. The multi-item cart checkout keeps its sign-in wall because a logged-out visitor cannot have a cart at all: _wpss_cart is user meta and add-to-cart requires login.
checkout_account_creation.password: Never asked for. create_account() generates one and wp_new_user_notification() sends WordPress's own set-password mail - core's, because it carries a single-use key and re-implementing that is how resets get broken.
checkout_account_creation.verified_2026_08_17: Logged-out purchase of service 544 with the offline rail: account created (display name from billing first+last), signed in, order 3171 inserted with customer_id = 71, payment_method recorded, order visible in the buyer's own dashboard with payment instructions, billing + first_name/last_name meta persisted, role subscriber, set-password mail sent. Collision: same email again stayed on checkout with the login link, no duplicate user, no order, no charge. Setting OFF: wall returns and the endpoint answers 403. Rate limit blocks attempt 21. REST /auth/register works with email only and returns an app-password token. 390px: note and fields full-width, no horizontal scroll.

api_shapes._note: Basecamp 10154919636. The API described the same thing differently depending on which endpoint you asked, so a client could not write one parser. Three shapes were in play: an actor, a date, and a service card. Every fix here is ADDITIVE - no key was removed or retyped - because src/API/API.php's contract_version rule is explicit that bumping bricks every build already shipped.
api_shapes.user_shape: wpss_rest_user() - one actor shape {id,name,avatar,deleted} everywhere. Routed in 8d8b4cd (services[].vendor, order vendor/customer) and extended here.
api_shapes.date_shape: RestController::format_datetime() for controllers, wpss_rest_date() for the global shape helpers. Both emit ISO-8601 with offset. Ten emissions across NotificationsController, ReviewsController, DisputesController, BuyerRequestsController, ProposalsController and VendorsController were emitting bare 'Y-m-d H:i:s' with no zone, so a client needed two parsers and had to GUESS the timezone for half the API. DisputesController carried a third implementation of its own (a local $format_date closure) - removed. Second pass: /me and /auth/me emitted user_registered raw (API.php, AuthController::format_user) - missed first time because the audit probed collection endpoints only. Both now ISO.
api_shapes.card_shape: wpss_rest_service_card() in src/functions/rest.php - THE service card. ServicesController::prepare_item_for_response() used to write this inline, which is why FavoritesController could not reuse it: the pieces were PRIVATE methods on the controller, so /favorites invented a `thumbnail` string, a flat `price` and a flat `rating` float instead. The three private methods (get_service_images, get_service_rating, prepare_terms_for_response) are now global (wpss_rest_service_images, wpss_rest_service_rating, wpss_prepare_term_for_rest) and the controller delegates. Verified byte-identical: /services returns the same 16 keys with the same sub-shapes as before the extraction. /favorites now returns all 16 canonical keys, with its legacy thumbnail/price/price_minor/currency merged ON TOP so nothing shipped breaks.
api_shapes.contract_version: NOT bumped. Per src/API/API.php: bump when a FIELD changes shape or meaning, never for a value change. An ISO date in a field that already held a date is a value change. Clients refuse a contract newer than the one they understand, so a bump would brick shipped builds.
api_shapes.residual_difference: ONE key could not be unified: /favorites `rating` is a float where the canonical shape is {average,count}. Same name, different TYPE - the one case where additive is impossible, since a client calling rating.toFixed() would crash on an object. Stays a float until the next contract_version bump; deleting the four lines in FavoritesController is the whole fix. It also reads the cached _wpss_rating_average meta where the canonical shape counts approved reviews live, so the two can disagree. Second, smaller: /favorites `excerpt` stays trimmed to 20 words where /services returns it whole - lengthening text a shipped app already lays out is not a silent change.
api_shapes.html_in_json: KEPT, not removed - reviews.review_html/created_human/vendor_reply_html/vendor_reply_human and messages.html. Removing a key is a shape change and would brick shipped builds. Not needed anyway: core's _fields query arg already trims them, measured over real HTTP at 8547->1825 bytes on /reviews (79% smaller) and 26867->6829 on /conversations/{id}/messages (75%). NOTE _fields is applied in rest_post_dispatch, which rest_do_request does NOT run - testing it through wp eval-file shows no reduction and is a false negative. Test over HTTP.
